supporting_observations.claim: WS-RIYER-01 made repeated connections to the proxy at roughly five-minute intervals during the alert window, including records at 13:35:56, 13:40:29, 13:45:50, 13:50:33, 13:55:37, 14:00:15, and 14:05:05 UTC.

At 14:05 UTC, kim.ortega requested a Kerberos ticket for FILE-LV-01 from the address assigned in the records to WS-RIYER-01, and FILE-LV-01 recorded a network logon for kim.ortega from that same address. This is inconsistent with the inventory’s stated practice that remote administration is only done from WS-KORTEGA-01, but does not by itself establish what action occurred on FILE-LV-01.

The domain controller recorded NTLM credential validation for raj.iyer with workstation names FILE-LV-01 and WS-DWELLS-01 during the review period. The records do not establish why those validations occurred.

The recurring proxy connections could be consistent with the approved DataGrid updater’s roughly five-minute update checks, but the supplied connection records do not identify the process or requested destination, so that explanation is unverified.

known_telemetry_limitations: The recurring connections are recorded as traffic to the explicit proxy on port 8080; those records do not identify the external HTTPS host or the initiating process.
The supplied proxy records identify destinations for some other connections, but do not provide destination details for the recurring connections in the alert window.
The FILE-LV-01 logon record establishes a network logon by kim.ortega from WS-RIYER-01’s address, not the specific action performed or whether it was remote administration.
The authentication validation records do not establish the purpose or authorization of raj.iyer’s credential use from the named workstations.
claims_not_established: That the recurring proxy connections were generated by dgupdate.exe or by malicious software.
That the recurring connections reached an unapproved or malicious external service.
That kim.ortega’s credentials were stolen or that the FILE-LV-01 logon resulted in an administrative action.
That raj.iyer’s credential validations from FILE-LV-01 or WS-DWELLS-01 were unauthorized.
That the scheduled svc-reporting password rotation caused or explains the observed activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy records for the recurring connections with destination hostnames, full timestamps, and any available TLS or request metadata.
Endpoint process-to-network telemetry on WS-RIYER-01 around each recurring connection, including process image, command line, signature, and file hash.
FILE-LV-01 audit and endpoint records around 14:05 UTC showing the resource accessed and any commands or changes associated with kim.ortega’s logon.
Confirmation from the change record and IT activity logs of whether kim.ortega used WS-RIYER-01 or accessed FILE-LV-01 at that time.
Authentication and endpoint records for the raj.iyer validations attributed to FILE-LV-01 and WS-DWELLS-01, to determine the initiating activity.
